ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: PP2
SUBJECT: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

2. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Toileting PRACTICES? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Toileting PRACTICES.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Toileting PRACTICES.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Toileting PRACTICES.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Toileting PRACTICES.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care for PRACTICES be able to;? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Care for PRACTICES be able to;.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care for PRACTICES be able to;.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Care for PRACTICES be able to;.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care for PRACTICES be able to;.

5. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

6. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Our ENVIRONMENT? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Our ENVIRONMENT.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Our ENVIRONMENT.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Our ENVIRONMENT.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Our ENVIRONMENT.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying PRACTICES? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for PRACTICES.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to PRACTICES.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on PRACTICES.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about PRACTICES.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying People found at home? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on People found at home.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to People found at home.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for People found at home.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about People found at home.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care PRACTICES? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Care PRACTICES.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Care PRACTICES.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care PRACTICES.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care PRACTICES.

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Overgrazing continuously

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Neighbourhood ENVIRONMENT? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Neighbourhood ENVIRONMENT.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Neighbourhood ENVIRONMENT.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Neighbourhood ENVIRONMENT.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Neighbourhood ENVIRONMENT.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Plants ENVIRONMENT and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Animals ENVIRONMENT and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Weather ENVIRONMENT and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Water ENVIRONMENT and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
